content: This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice and should not replace the guidance of your healthcare professional. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Before starting treatment with vedolizumab, ensure that your vaccinations are up to date. This medication is administered via intravenous injection by a healthcare professional, and the infusion should be given slowly over 30 minutes. After the initial dose, subsequent doses are typically administered at 2 weeks and 6 weeks, followed by maintenance doses every 8 weeks. Infusion reactions may occur during or several hours after the administration of this drug. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms such as shortness of breath, rapid heartbeat, or flushing. Use this medication consistently to achieve the maximum benefit. Common side effects may include nausea, headache, flu-like symptoms, or fatigue. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of potential side effects. However, this medication may suppress your immune system, increasing your susceptibility to infections or worsening existing infections. It may also elevate the risk of a rare but serious brain infection called progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML), which can be fatal in some cases. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. If you experience symptoms of an allergic reaction, such as rash, itching, swelling, severe dizziness, or difficulty breathing, seek immediate medical attention. This is not an exhaustive list of potential side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar guidance. Before using vedolizumab, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other complications. Avoid contact with individuals who have contagious infections, such as chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, or the flu. Inform your doctor about your vaccination history and discuss whether you need any vaccines before starting this medication. Notify your healthcare provider that you are using vedolizumab before receiving any immunizations or vaccinations. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is known to pass into breast milk, so consult your doctor about the risks and benefits if you are breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, if the individual has severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and medical tests, such as endoscopy or liver function tests, may be conducted while you are using this medication. Ensure that you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, it is important to receive the next dose as soon as possible according to the prescribed schedule. Storage instructions are not applicable for this medication, as it is administered in a clinical setting. Your medical condition may lead to complications in a medical emergency. Always carry relevant medical information and inform healthcare providers about your condition. This information was last revised in May 2024.
